annotations.title: utilpeek: verify a JWT signature and claims with a secret, a PEM public key or a JWK Set

description: utilpeek: Verify a JWT signature and claims. To read the claims without a key use decode_jwt. Returns valid true or false for a JWT checked with PyJWT against one key (HMAC secret, PEM public key or JWK Set), with a reason: bad signature, expired, wrong audience or issuer, algorithm not allowed. Algorithm none is refused; the key type fixes the algorithm family. Input: `token` and exactly one of `secret`, `public_key` or `jwks`; optional `algorithms`, `audience`, `issuer`, `leeway_seconds`. Pure computation, no network; secrets and keys are not echoed. A failed check is a normal charged result (valid false). No JWKS URL fetch: send the key set. Malformed input is a 422 (not charged). Typically under 0.1 s. Price: USD 0.001. Free: 10 utilpeek calls per IP per UTC day. The submitted text is never logged or stored. Docs: https://tanod.dev/learn/jwt-decode-verify-api.html

algorithms.description: Allow-list that narrows the default for the key type; none is refused.
algorithms.title: Algorithms

audience.description: Required aud (a string, or a list of which one must match).
audience.title: Audience

jwks.description: JWK Set object {"keys": [...]} (asymmetric keys; oct keys are ignored). The key is picked by the token kid.
jwks.title: Jwks

leeway_seconds.description: Clock skew allowed for exp, nbf and iat (0-300).
leeway_seconds.title: Leeway Seconds

public_key.description: PEM public key (RS*, PS*, ES*, EdDSA).
public_key.title: Public Key
